reason: IIS sends Server: Microsoft-IIS/10.0; webForCore's host is Kestrel.
A static file is served by ASP.NET's static file handler (IIS: its static file module), which sends no Accept-Ranges: bytes.
A static file is served by ASP.NET's static file handler (IIS: its static file module), which sends Cache-Control: public.
A static file is served by ASP.NET's static file handler (IIS: its static file module), whose ETag has another form.
A static file is served by ASP.NET's static file handler (IIS: its static file module), whose Last-Modified the worker request leaves out (as Cassini, which it comes from, did).
A static file, or a 404 for one, is ASP.NET's (IIS: its static file module's), so it has X-AspNet-Version.
A file that doesn't exist gets ASP.NET's 404 page; IIS serves its native 404.0 page (StaticFile handler). The status is 404 on both.
Request filtering's 404.11 (a double escape, or '+') is webForCore's short IIS error page; IIS sends its detailed error page. Same status and substatus.
Request filtering's 404.11 is webForCore's short IIS error page (text/html); IIS's detailed error page is text/html; charset=utf-8.
IIS's detailed error page for request filtering's 404.11 has Cache-Control: private; webForCore's has none.
IIS closes the connection after request filtering's 404.11; webForCore keeps it open.

ASP.NET's 400 for a character of requestPathInvalidCharacters is the same error page, with webForCore's source file, line, stack frames (from its PDBs) and version information instead of .NET Framework's.
